messages.subject: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
messages.subject_clean: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The help file (new summary scantwo Oct 2006) says that scantwo uses the output of the single qtl model from scanone.  I have run multiple scantwo and scanone analyses using Haley-Knott regression, EM, and multiple imputation.  How do I know if my scantwo output (say from multiple imputations) is using the correct scanone output (also from multiple imputations)?  Do I need to use particular filenames or run these analyses back to back?

thanks

Tarek

***************************************
Tarek Elnaccash
Program in ecology & evolution
University of Pittsburgh
Department of Biological Sciences
4249 Fifth Ave.
Pittsburgh, PA 15260

messages.body_plain:
Scantwo also performs the relevant single-dimensional scan with
scanone, so the results contain the relevant scanone results.  There
are no worries about object or file names or such.

karl

messages.subject: problems with cim
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl (et. al)

Thanks for adding the cim function; it is nice to be able to compare the different methods all within R/qtl

We have run into what I think is a bug in the current cim implementation: when there are more than 1 QTL per chromosome, cim often returns NA for most of the LOD scores on that chromosome.  I believe that this happens when both QTL in the same chromosome are used as marker covariates.

The following code will usually reproduce the problem.  It depends some on the particular simulation instance, so if you don't see it the first time, try again.

Also, while it may appear from the simulations that this only happens when one is using more marker covariates than appropriate, in our real data we had it happen with fewer convariates than QTL.

Thanks again for all of the hard work on R/qtl.  It is a really nice pacakge.

All the best,

Julin

###################################

model <- matrix(c(
		2,40,.8,0,
		7,13,1.1,0,
		7,75,1,0),byrow=T,ncol=4)

cross <- sim.cross(map,n.ind=200,model=model)

#plot(cross)

cross <- calc.genoprob(cross,step=2)

out.ehk <- scanone(cross,method="ehk")

par(mfrow=c(3,2))

plot(out.ehk,main="ehk")

for (i in 1:5) {
	print(paste("number of marker covariates: ",i))
	out.cim <-cim(cross,n.marcovar=i)
	plot(out.cim,main=i)
	print(out.cim[is.na <http://is.na>(out.cim$lod),])
	}

--
Julin Maloof
Assistant Professor
Section of Plant Biology
University of California, Davis
1 Shields Ave
Davis, CA, 95616

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] problems with cim
messages.body_plain:
Dear Julin,

I think I've identified and fixed the bug; I'll incorporate the fix
into the next version of R/qtl.

I've realized that there's another problem with the CIM function: in
the case of an intercross,
we assume additivity of alleles for the marker covariates, putting in
a single column for each
marker.  This is also done in the forward selection.  I'll work on
that for the next version of R/qtl.

Also, the X chromosome is not treated specially, and needs to be.
I'll leave that for the future.

regards,
karl
-----------
Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu
http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman
